result.title: Anticipating Social Consequences with Distributional World Models
result.summary: Social world models predict how interactions develop after an action, helping agents negotiate, cooperate and mediate. In these situations, one action can lead to several plausible futures, hence predicting only one future can overlook consequential alternatives, while exploring them through repeated simulations increases inference cost. We propose DSWM, a Distributional Social World Model that predicts alternative responses, their probabilities and immediate and final outcome values in one output per candidate action. We train a 4B model on repeated simulations using supervised fine-tuning and GRPO. At inference time, the actor uses these possible consequences to choose an action. Across three seen and two unseen environments, with interaction backbones absent from training collection, DSWM achieves the best average performance on 13 of 15 metrics. Ablations show that retaining multiple futures and their predicted probabilities improves outcomes in all five environments.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DSWM 分布式社会世界模型：对每个候选动作一次性输出多种可能的他人回应、各自概率以及即时与最终结果价值，用重复模拟数据经 SFT 与 GRPO 训练 4B 模型，推理时由 actor 依据这些可能后果选择动作。
AI.relevance_reason: 「同时保留多条未来并给出概率再做决策」的表述可能为 LVR 中多 latent 假设的表示、概率化筛选与基于预期价值的停止/选择提供参照，但该工作无视觉输入也无显式推理状态，属远领域线索，需核查其概率与价值头是否可迁移。
